Use N-mm-MPa units.
Assume Euler-Bernoulli beam theory with small deflection and linear elastic behavior.
Model a cantilever beam of length L = 1800 mm fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L.
Use structural steel with E = 200000 MPa.
Use constant second moment of area I = 1200000 mm^4.
Apply a downward point load P = 2000 N at the free end.
Do not assume zero rotation at the free end and do not assume constant moment over the span.
Use the standard cantilever formulas: free-end slope theta = P L^2 / (2 E I) and free-end deflection delta = P L^3 / (3 E I).
Report the slope at the free end in radians and degrees.
Report the vertical deflection at the free end in mm.
The slope at the free end is 0.0135 rad or 0.773 degrees downward.
The vertical deflection at the free end is 16.2 mm downward.
